title: The Spirit of truth (John 16:1–15)
hookLine: the Advocate will guide you into all truth

lines: SOMEONE COMES AND STANDS BESIDE YOU.
cards: An ancient courtroom. You've been accused, and you're standing alone. Then someone walks in and stands beside you.
Not the judge. Not a hired gun who talks over you. A friend of good standing who comes alongside and speaks up for you.
The Greeks had a word for that person. Jesus has just told his friends that the world may turn against them. Now he tells them who will be standing beside them when it does.

teach.h: PARAKLETOS: ONE CALLED TO YOUR SIDE.
teach.b: The word is parakletos. Para means beside, and kletos means called: one called to your side. In a courtroom, that's an advocate.
The King James Bible translates it Comforter, and in older English, comfort carried a sense of strengthening, not only soothing. Other translations say Helper, Counselor, Advocate.
No single English word holds it all, which is why some people simply say Paraclete. Here's the surprise.

teach.h: IT IS BETTER FOR YOU THAT I GO.
teach.b: Jesus tells his friends it's good that he's leaving. "It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you." Expedient means better for you.
Then something tender: "I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now." He doesn't dump everything on them at once.
And then the promise in today's carry: "when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth."

teach.h: HE WILL GUIDE YOU INTO ALL TRUTH.
teach.b: Guide. The Greek word has the sense of leading someone along a way: not dropping all the answers at once, but walking you there. Christians understand this promise in several ways.

Catholic and Orthodox Christians see the Spirit guiding the whole church through its teaching and tradition over the centuries. Many Protestants emphasize the Spirit opening the scriptures to believers as they read.
Pentecostal Christians speak of the Spirit's guidance as close and present, in daily life. In each, the promise is that they are not left to work things out on their own.
This week: many rooms, show us the Father, my peace, the vine, called friends, a warning, and now the Advocate.

how: Christians often pray for the Holy Spirit's guidance before decisions, meetings and the reading of scripture, and many churches celebrate the Spirit's coming at Pentecost.

games.q: you're about to leave your friends, and they're afraid. what do you tell them?
o: stay here and wait for me.
it's better for you that I go, so the Advocate can come.
games.why: "It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you."

practice: Bring to mind one choice in front of you right now, large or small, and don't try to solve it; just hold it, the way you'd hold a map before a walk, noticing what you already know and what you can't bear to know yet.
If you pray, ask the Spirit to lead you one step on the road, not the whole way at once; if not, simply ask yourself what the next honest step would be.
